# Managed SQLite source backport

Arcanum builds this provider from the exact Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core10.0.10 source recorded in `source-manifest.json`. The upstream tree/license come from official VMR commit `f7d90799ce4ef09a0bb257852a57248d2a8fb8dd`. Only `upstream/SqliteDataRecord.cs` differs: `null-origin.patch` retains the early null-origin cached-MemoryStream guard present in immutable EF commit `493b52c681ba7f9a25c7a2e6c89d237f735c83c4`. No other main/release changes are imported. All33 upstream C# files otherwise stay byte-identical; upstream formatting is retained outside first-party `src/`.

The same package ID/version satisfies EF's existing dependency through a ProjectReference. EF10.0.10 and PCL2.1.11 are unchanged; a second official provider assembly must not enter restore/runtime/AOT output. The provider targets net8.0, matching the original NuGet asset's compilation surface. Assembly identity stays `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite, Version=10.0.10.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=adb9793829ddae60`.

This is an **Arcanum self-built, public-signed** binary, not a Microsoft-signed release. The160-byte public key was extracted without loading code from the original pinned assembly; it contains no Microsoft private key. Public-signing preserves reference identity, not publisher authentication. Informational version `10.0.10+arcanum.null-origin.1`, Company and assembly metadata identify the self-built backport. Do not package or publish this project as an official Microsoft NuGet release (`IsPackable=false`).

Build with the repository-selected SDK and record its exact compiler/runtime version: `dotnet build vendor/Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core/Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core.csproj -c Release -t:Rebuild`. `source-hashes.props` closes the compile inventory and verifies all upstream source/resource/license/public-key hashes before PrepareForBuild. Unknown C# inputs or changed bytes fail. Root-owned build properties pin the target/compiler/assembly/deterministic/public-sign/path-map behavior; no source download or patch application runs during an ordinary build. Repeating the same controlled rebuild is qualified separately; no bit identity with Microsoft's private-signed release is claimed.

Upstream refresh is a reviewed source/provenance change. Fetch the exact manifest URLs/commit, verify Git blob and SHA256 for every input, retain the MIT license, then apply only the reviewed guard and update its compiled-file SHA in both manifest and props. Preserve independent original-public-API baseline and actual child-process crash controls. Never replace the guard with native API armor, a false metadata result, or a whole-array wrapper for every table BLOB. Ordinary table rowid reads retain real SqliteBlob streaming.
